summary: Markets are displaying a mixed but cautiously optimistic mood, with Asian shares and bonds bouncing while the dollar pulled back as a pause in US-Iran hostilities eased immediate geopolitical tensions. The dominant macro drivers this week are the anticipated Federal Reserve decision, with Kalshi traders closely parsing what incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh may signal, alongside the de-escalation between the US and Iran that has sent oil prices sharply lower and boosted safe-haven assets like gold over 1%. At the stock level, Apple reclaimed its position as the world's most valuable company by passing Nvidia, whose outlook was further clouded by reports of a potential $250 billion backstop for OpenAI raising fresh concerns about AI trade valuations, while Boeing and JetBlue drew attention for contrasting structural moves and Corning diverged sharply from Boeing's trajectory. The key risk factors investors are monitoring include the fragility of the US-Iran ceasefire — underscored by Iran's foreign minister warning that Ukraine's attack on an Iranian vessel "cannot go unanswered" — ongoing Red Sea shipping disruptions following a Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, and uncertainty around Fed Chair Warsh's policy tone. In the short term, the market's direction will hinge on the Fed's guidance and whether geopolitical tensions remain contained, with rotation from tech into industrials and other sectors likely to continue if AI sentiment stays under pressure.
